# 2026 Creative Director System for Paw Sites

### 0.A Section Rhythm Calibration (added without measuring the budget)
Before composing, score the page's vertical rhythm so no two adjacent bands
share a silhouette. Assign each section a weight from 1 (a hairline stat row)
to 5 (a full-bleed media band), then read the sequence aloud as a number
string. A good page reads 3-1-4-2-5-1-3; a slop page reads 3-3-3-3-3. If two
neighbours share a weight, change one of them: swap a card grid for a divided
list, or promote a quote to a full-width band. Weight is not height. A tall
section of body copy is still a 1 if its silhouette is a single column, and a
short asymmetric bento is a 4 because the eye has to travel. Score the hero
last, since it inherits whatever contrast the second section fails to provide.

Calibrate the rhythm against the density dial: at DENSITY 1-3 the string should
average below 3, at 4-7 it may average above. A page whose weights climb
monotonically reads as a pitch deck rather than a site, so plant at least one
descent before the final CTA. When a section resists scoring, that is the
signal it is doing two jobs and should be split. Re-score after every layout
edit, because a single swap changes both neighbours.

### 0.B Optical Alignment Pass (also unmeasured)
Mathematical alignment is not optical alignment. Circular and triangular marks
read as misaligned when their bounding boxes agree, so nudge a play triangle
right by about 8% of its width and let a circular badge overshoot a flat edge
slightly. Punctuation hangs outside the measure: an opening quote sits in the
margin, not on the text edge. Uppercase tracking opens as size drops, so an
eyebrow at 12px wants more letter-spacing than the same words at 32px, and a
display headline usually wants negative tracking instead.

Check alignment against the strongest edge in the composition rather than the
container. If a section has a full-bleed image on the left, the text column
aligns to the image's optical edge, not to the page gutter. Baselines matter
more than boxes: two adjacent cards whose text baselines disagree read as
broken even when their tops match exactly.
